findings.text: The field response blocks have no production builder: poloidal_field consumes them, but no code under nova/ constructs a PrescribedCurrentField carrying them - the operator only accepts a caller-supplied instance (line 2200), and every construction in the tree is a test (tests/test_equilibrium_diagnostics.py:576, tests/test_equilibrium_forward_operator.py:215,314,320) or the uncommitted timing driver. So 'built once at operator build' describes machinery that no production route builds, and the receipt's grid_imaged_route_exercised true rests on tests and the driver alone. The wiring is plausibly the deferred constraint.py work, but nothing in the node says so.

The reuse test counts the fixture's own constructions rather than a solve's: built_count = len(kernel_evaluations) samples the spy appended inside _field_response's interaction() closure, which the test itself invokes nine times (line 238 asserts 9), and line 249 then asserts the two poloidal_field calls added none. That is a valid no-kernel-on-evaluation control, but it is not the required 'the build runs once and a second solve reuses it' - no operator build, no second solve and no cache path is exercised, so a build that repeated on every solve would still pass this test.

exact_biot_kernel_evaluations_per_field_evaluation: 0 is a hardcoded literal (driver at /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/nova/s19-codex/shafranov-field-responses/measure_timing.py, not committed to the repository). The claim is true - reading poloidal_field shows the evaluation is matmuls and a stencil only - but the receipt presents a measured-looking pair in which one half is asserted; the 76 is likewise the driver's own counter (lines 45/54/77), and the timing runs on a 64-node surrogate lattice with 12 conductor rectangles, so the 114199x ratio is a surrogate ratio the receipt does not label as one.

The gate asserts order > 0.5 while the order itself, computed at line 69, is never printed or persisted, so the one number the brief asked the route to report reaches no reader. Measured first-hand on the same route: relative errors 7.4717e-1, 4.9018e-1 and 3.5775e-1 at 21/31/41 nodes with 501/1001/2001 contour points, fitted order 1.1007 (21->41), 1.0823 and 1.1264 for the adjacent pairs - first-order-like, not the second order a fixed-weight interpolation of a smooth field onto a shrinking grid should approach, and still 36% off the volume definition at the finest resolution tested. A 0.5 floor therefore sits well below the measured value at every resolution and cannot discriminate a first-order route from a second-order one; whether the shortfall comes from the stencil degenerating on lattice-edge nodes or from the 5% margin is not isolated here, and the receipt's top-level fitted_order 0.3529 belongs to the pre-existing contour rows rather than to this route.

The manifest's follow_ons names a single pre-existing failure here (test_solve_none_reproduces_the_stored_vector_bit_identically); at base c3801e9a two fail - that one and test_solve_and_solve_branch_trace_prescribed_current_replacements (line 101), both AttributeError: '_LinearTarget' object has no attribute 'null' at forward_operator.py:2237 in the base tree - and both fail identically at HEAD, so the attribution is correct but the inventory is short by one test.

justifications.durability: Folding the response digest into geometry_identity closes a real aliasing gap on this base: before this change no prescribed-response component entered the identity, so two operators carrying different field responses shared one cache and one jit program key. The pytree threading is complete (ten children, aux booleans for the optional plasma blocks) and the positive control in the reuse test (built_count == 9) is a genuine guard that would catch a missing construction. Point held back because the receipt's numbers have no committed driver - measure_timing.py exists only in the run reports directory, so the timing half cannot be regenerated from the repository - and because tree_unflatten rebuilds through object.__new__ (:1742), so a reconstructed instance never re-runs the __post_init__ validation that guards paired presence, equal shapes and shared grid rows.
justifications.evidence: The gate reproduces first-hand in one all_debug job through the shared interpreter (JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu, 70 passed in 168.41 s, EXIT=0), matching the node's 156.24 s, and receipt.json carries exactly the fence's numbers: 76 build calls, 0 per evaluation, build 7.1573 s, median 62.67 us over 31 samples, ratio 114199x, toroidal volume from the solved state's own integral, grid_imaged_route_exercised true. The timing SVG read as text repeats the same three claims (title, the two bar values, '76 kernel calls at build; 0 per evaluation', ratio 114199x). Deductions: the per-evaluation zero is a literal written by the driver rather than a measurement; the ratio is measured on a 64-node surrogate lattice with 12 conductor rectangles and the receipt does not label it a surrogate; the convergence order the brief asked to be reported is not persisted, and the receipt's top-level fitted_order 0.3529 belongs to the pre-existing contour rows, so a reader cannot tell which route it scores; and the manifest names one pre-existing failure in tests/test_prescribed_current_solve.py where two fail identically at base.
justifications.fit: Lands beside the flux response in the module that already owns the operator's cache identity, reuses the mesh's own fixed-weight stencil rather than adding an interpolator, and every added symbol is behaviour-named (PoloidalField, radial_response, vertical_response, plasma_radial_response, plasma_vertical_response, has_field_response, grid_poloidal_field, boundary_poloidal_field) with no plan label and no version suffix. Deductions: the three plasma-moment blocks are carried as a bare three-tuple whose order only __post_init__ shape checks pin, where a named carrier would make the cell-current / radial first-moment / vertical first-moment order self-describing; and the object.__new__ unflatten noted above.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The build-once machinery is delivered as written and verified by reading the code path: the radial and vertical field blocks are fixed-shape pytree leaves of PrescribedCurrentField (forward_operator.py:1714 flatten, :1742 unflatten, ten children), their digest folds into _compute_geometry_identity under prescribed_response_identity (:2439), and per evaluation poloidal_field (:1675) performs only radial_response @ conductor, vertical_response @ conductor and the three plasma-moment block products. No Biot kernel and no flux gradient appears anywhere on the imaging path or the contour interpolation, which composes grid_poloidal_field (:3635), interpolate_grid_poloidal_field (:3659, the mesh's own shared_node_flux_stencil at :3677) and boundary_poloidal_field (:3680). The analytic grid-imaged case is built at 21/31/41 nodes, and item (3) is named unfinished rather than claimed. Two requirements fall short as written: the test that 'the build runs once and a second solve reuses it' measures the fixture's own synthetic constructions rather than a build-then-solve reuse, and the convergence order the brief asked the route to report is computed but never emitted, so the receipt does not carry it.
justifications.scope_discipline: Two commits touching only declared paths: 796df350 changes nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py and the two test modules, a00ea1ad adds the PNG/SVG pair, the receipt, the plan landing record and the cumulative evidence section. Item (3) (ExternalShafranovConstraint.observed and the benchmark) is named unfinished under follow_ons rather than reached for, and the timing driver stays outside the repository in the run reports directory. No plan, sprint or ticket identifier appears in any added symbol, filename or comment; both commits carry a body stating what changed and why, and neither carries an attribution trailer.
